subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: On normal gateway stop or SIGTERM, should OpenClaw terminate active supervised exec child processes, preserve background and active exec work, or add a narrower opt-in and diagnostic shutdown policy?
rationale: Current tests intentionally preserve active runs on normal shutdown, while the report shows referenced child-process handles can force dirty shutdown; automation should not choose the product boundary between cleanup and preserving user-started background work.

options.title: Bound foreground cancellation
options.body: Cancel non-background active supervised exec work during normal shutdown, preserve explicit background sessions unless separately killed, and emit diagnostics for remaining handles.

options.title: Kill all supervised exec
options.body: Make gateway stop a hard lifecycle boundary that terminates all supervised exec children before exit.

options.title: Preserve current default
options.body: Keep background and active exec preservation as the default and add diagnostics or operator commands while accepting that long children can still cause dirty shutdown.

recommendation.title: Bound foreground cancellation
recommendation.body: Cancel non-background active supervised exec work during normal shutdown, preserve explicit background sessions unless separately killed, and emit diagnostics for remaining handles.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged shutdown fix and already separated this issue from the websocket shutdown blocker in the issue discussion.
